sentence: This project studies how liver health affects aging of the heart, brain, and bone in mouse models, using imaging and molecular profiling.
This project uses statistical methods to sort patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome, pneumonia, and sepsis into phenotypes.
This project tests a personalized way to place electrodes and use brain stimulation to control seizures in epilepsy.
This project tests when and for how long to give hepatitis C virus medications to people receiving kidneys from infected donors.
This project studies how cannabinoid exposure during adolescence affects the development of brain neurotransmitter systems and executive function.
This project studies how mitochondrial function and DNA methylation relate to aging in people with HIV, and whether exercise can reverse the damage.
This project uses skin epithelium as a model to study how stem cells interact with their surroundings to renew and survive.
This project studies how genetic differences change alternative splicing in human airway epithelial cells and raise the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
This project studies whether positive emotions help older adults with mild cognitive impairment handle negative emotions caused by stress.
This project uses imaging to study how bladder cancer cells take different paths to divide and how neighboring cells affect this.
This project builds a pipeline to find chromatin marks linked to aging and to make reagents that detect them.
This project expands models to study how often multiple myeloma occurs and to test ways to prevent, find early, and treat it.
This project tests whether red blood cell capillary velocity can be used as a laboratory test for a poorly understood, complex disease.
This project develops a method to image glycogen in muscle on clinical MRI scanners.
This project studies how glioblastoma tumors resist therapy and looks for a way to treat them.
This project builds an imaging tool that shows how large molecules such as proteins move and interact in water.
This project studies why people respond differently to the same treatment, using causal machine learning.
This project combines two core facilities into one that offers microscopy, mass spectrometry, and structural biology services to researchers.
